medicaid_sensitivity.assumptions: The pre-period is informative about the size of post-period violations; only two pre-period steps are available, and both are estimated with error
medicaid_sensitivity.estimand: Average effect of the January 2014 expansion on the uninsured share in the expansion cohort, 2014–2019
medicaid_sensitivity.estimator: Year-by-year event-study coefficients from Chapter 6's PERWT-weighted regression with state and year fixed effects; identified sets formed as coefficient ± (years since 2013) × M̄ × (largest pre-period step)

identification.assumption: Parallel trends between cohort and comparison states; no anticipation; no spillovers across states
identification.claim_type: Causal by assumption, not by design
identification.made_true_by: Argument. States chose expansion; nothing in the design makes the comparison states' trend the cohort's counterfactual
identification.observed: State-year uninsured shares in the cohort and comparison states, before and after 2014
identification.sensitivity: At the point estimates the average effect's identified set reaches zero when each post-period step of the violation is about three times the largest pre-period step
identification.without_assumption: Unbounded. With the relative-magnitudes restriction, the identified set widens in proportion to M̄ and the years since 2013

medicaid_sensitivity.implicit_weights: As in Chapter 6; the average over years weights the six post-period coefficients equally
medicaid_sensitivity.target_population: Civilian and military household population ages 19–64 with family income at or below 138% of the poverty threshold, in the 30 design states of Chapter 6, 2011–2019
medicaid_sensitivity.title: Medicaid expansion and uninsurance: how much the conclusion leans on parallel trends
medicaid_sensitivity.variance_estimator: None. Evaluated at the point estimates; HonestDiD confidence sets that add state-clustered sampling uncertainty are planned

turnout_bounds.assumptions: Reported votes are taken at face value, although surveys overstate voting; people outside the CPS frame (institutions, active military) are outside every bound
turnout_bounds.estimand: Share who reported voting; the White minus Black difference in that share
turnout_bounds.estimator: Identities in observed weighted components: lower bound r·v, upper bound r·v + (1 − r), where r is the share answering and v the rate among them
turnout_bounds.explicit_weights: VOSUPPWT (CPS Voting and Registration Supplement weight), equal to the basic monthly weight for every citizen adult it counts

identification.assumption: None for the bounds. The Census convention adds: no nonrespondent voted. The respondents-only convention adds: within each group, nonrespondents voted at the respondents' rate
identification.made_true_by: Neither convention is made true by the design. The supplement weight does not adjust for people who skipped the voting questions
identification.observed: The weighted share who answered the voting question and the reported voting rate among them, by group
identification.sensitivity: The gap is zero only if Black nonrespondents voted at a much higher rate than White nonrespondents; no common rate erases it
identification.without_assumption: Turnout lies between the Census-convention rate and that rate plus the nonresponse share; the gap lies in an interval as wide as the two groups' nonresponse shares added together

turnout_bounds.randomness: CPS sampling of households; not quantified here, because the extract carries no design information (Chapter 1)
turnout_bounds.target_population: U.S. citizens 18 and older in the civilian noninstitutional population, not in the armed forces, November 2020; and the non-Hispanic White and non-Hispanic Black citizens among them
turnout_bounds.title: What the 2020 CPS identifies about turnout, and what it leaves to assumption
turnout_bounds.variance_estimator: None attached. Bounds address missing answers; sampling intervals around each bound are a separate, planned addition
